correctness.rationale: Cut enumeration conditional on a positive hub gives the per-pair factor A=1+2uz+uz²; reversal gives B=u+2uz+z² and a factor z at the negative hub. Independently, B has the two conjugate roots a=−u±i√(u(1−u)) of modulus √u<1, so z(B/A)^m is a finite Blaschke product on the disk, with a strictly increasing boundary phase. Its equation with −1 gives exactly 2m+1 distinct simple zeros. Writing w=z^−1 A(z) on the circle gives phase derivative −(1−u)(1+u+2u cos θ)/|w|² for arg w. The arc-count discrepancy from normalized unwrapped phase increment is O(1/(2m+1)), so the limit is the stated positive, normalized density. After extracting positive factors the derivative in c=cos θ has numerator −4uc²−4(u+1)c+3u²−6u−1; it decreases strictly with c and has endpoint signs + at −1, − at 1. Its sole admissible zero is the stated c_u, yielding exactly two maxima and two strict endpoint minima on the circle. The first root satisfies 2m[−arg w(θ_m)]+θ_m=π. Taylor expansion gives the stated denominator from slope (1−u)/(1+3u); oddness and θ_m=O(m^−1) give the O_u(m^−3) angle error. A heterogeneous ordinary star quantizes the phase of z·prod_j[(z+q_j)/(1+q_j z)]; its normalized zero counts on arcs differ from the corresponding normalized phase increments by O(1/(n+1)). Empirical q-law subsequences converge on [0,1]; on compact subintervals of (0,π) the resulting Poisson-kernel mixture is nondecreasing, also when q→1 since its boundary limit there is zero and mass at q=1 can contribute only an atom at π. Thus the separation holds for arbitrary positive heterogeneous bonds, not just for parameters uniformly away from q=1. Separate exact cut enumerations for one and two petals match the polynomial.
residual_risks: All limits and error constants here use fixed u in (0,1); no uniform claim at either excluded boundary. Small enumeration does not establish the phase asymptotics or peak theorem.

originality.rationale: Circle location, simplicity for connected ferromagnets, phase quantization via Blaschke products, and the star-kernel mechanism are prior. The supported distinct claim is a two-peak transition in shape under triangle decoration at every fixed positive finite coupling, with exact peak locations and a strict obstruction to matching by heterogeneous ordinary stars. The generic methods do not by themselves determine this shape.
residual_risks: The targeted search and inspected prior passages do not exclude an unindexed friendship-graph or repeated-block calculation. No claim of exhaustive priority or a new circle/simplicity theorem.

value.rationale: The exact two-peak law demonstrates a qualitative change under a simple graph decoration, at every fixed positive coupling. More strongly, it rules out reproducing that change by arbitrary positive bond heterogeneity on the ordinary star. The density shape and closest-zero scale supply a useful exact high-degree comparison; circle location and finite simplicity alone would not justify the contribution.
residual_risks: No claim of a bulk phase transition or a general classification of decorated or bounded-degree graphs.
